headlines.title: 4 Dividend Kings Retirees Can Buy and Hold Forever: Safe Income for the Next 60 Years
headlines.summary: Four companies have raised their dividends every single year for decades, but one of them is now paying out nearly every dollar it earns, leaving almost no room for error if business gets worse.

headlines.title: Johnson & Johnson Launches Next-Generation Shockwave™ C2 Aero Fly Coronary IVL Catheter, Cutting IVL Treatment Time in Half
headlines.summary: SANTA CLARA, Calif., October 20, 2026--Next-generation IVL catheter delivers pulses at 2 Hz, improving efficiency in calcium modification treatment of coronary artery disease.

headlines.title: Johnson & Johnson’s Dividend Machine Is Running. Can Earnings Keep Up?
headlines.summary: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) stands out in the healthcare world for a reason. Its massive scale, strong research teams, and deep relationships with hospitals and medical professionals give it an edge that’s tough for competitors to match.

headlines.title: Ds vs. Dividend Stocks: One Protects Your Principal, the Other Could Grow Your Income
headlines.summary: A CD and a dividend stock can both pay you income in retirement, but they make very different promises, and breaking one of them could cost you far more than a lower yield.

headlines.title: 3 Dividend Kings to Buy Now for Protection Against Rising Rates
headlines.summary: A risk-free bond now pays enough to make most dividend stocks look pointless, but three companies have raised their payouts for over 50 straight years and carry betas low enough to sleep through a rate spike.

description: Johnson & Johnson, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the research and development, manufacture, and sale of a range of products in the healthcare field worldwide. It operates in two segments, Innovative Medicine and MedTech. The Innovative Medicine segment offers products for various therapeutic areas, such as oncology, immunology, neuroscience, pulmonary hypertension, infectious diseases, and cardiovascular and metabolism distributed through retailers, wholesalers, distributors, hospitals, and healthcare professionals for prescription use. The MedTech segment provides a portfolio of products used in the surgery, orthopedic, cardiovascular, and vision fields distributed through wholesalers, hospitals and retailers, and used in the professional fields by physicians, nurses, hospitals, eye care professionals and clinics. This segment also offers products and enabling technologies that support joint reconstruction, trauma, spine, sports related injuries, and others, as well as open, laparoscopic, and robotic surgical procedures; instrumentation, energy devices, stapling systems, wound closure, biosurgery products, and digital and robotic technologies; breast aesthetics and reconstruction; contact lenses under the ACUVUE brand; intraocular lenses for cataract surgery, and other products used in cataract and refractive procedures under the TECNIS brand. The company was founded in 1886 and is based in New Brunswick, New Jersey.
